title: Should AI Systems Explain Their Reasoning, or Only Their Conclusions?
topic: When should an AI assistant explain its reasoning, summarize it, cite evidence, expose uncertainty, or simply provide a conclusion?
brief: Use the source packet to create a concrete discussion about reasoning transparency. Avoid treating explanation as automatically good. Push the difference between useful auditability and persuasive rationalization.

source_packet.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0
source_packet.notes: Frames transparency, explainability, interpretability, reliability, and accountability as trustworthiness attributes.

source_packet.title: OpenAI Model Spec 2025-09-12
source_packet.notes: Discusses hidden chain-of-thought messages and tradeoffs around exposing raw reasoning.

source_packet.title: OpenAI Reasoning Models Guide
source_packet.notes: Describes reasoning models and reasoning summaries.

source_packet.title: Anthropic: Measuring Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
source_packet.notes: Raises the possibility that stated chains of thought may not faithfully reflect why an answer was produced.

source_packet.title: Google AI Principles
source_packet.notes: Connects explanation design to accountability, safety, privacy, and social benefit.

participants.name: OpenAI
participants.stance: Pragmatic about reasoning summaries, citations, and task-specific explanations. Wary of exposing raw hidden reasoning as a false transparency ritual.

participants.name: Anthropic
participants.stance: Cautious about persuasive rationalizations and unfaithful explanations. Prioritizes calibrated uncertainty and user trust over performative transparency.

participants.name: Google
participants.stance: Systems-oriented. Focuses on product context, evidence interfaces, citations, confidence signals, and how explanation formats shape user behavior.

editorial_goals: Make the distinction between raw reasoning, reasoning summaries, citations, and conclusions explicit.
Use at least three concrete examples.
Force disagreement about whether explanations increase trust or merely persuasion.
Let the visible moderator steer the discussion between rounds.
